reason: The sources provide over 15 verifiable claims supported by at least two distinct sites (Wikipedia, NASA, Scientific American, and LiveScience).
story: In 1977, NASA took advantage of a rare planetary alignment that occurs only once every 176 years. They launched Voyager 2 first, sixteen days before its twin, yet named it 'Voyager 2' because Voyager 1 was on a faster trajectory. While its twin grabbed headlines for reaching the gas giants first, Voyager 2 became the ultimate marathon runner. It remains the only spacecraft ever to visit the ice giants, Uranus and Neptune, where it discovered hidden rings and dozens of new moons. Today, the probe is over 12 billion miles away, operating on ancient technology with millions of times less memory than a modern cellphone. Because its path past Neptune sent it diving south, it can now only hear commands from a single antenna in Australia. Powered by decaying plutonium, it has officially entered interstellar space, acting as a silent ambassador for a world it left nearly half a century ago.
angle: Voyager 2 launched two weeks before Voyager 1 but was given the 'number 2' name because it took a slower, longer path to become the only probe to visit the ice giants.

claims.claim: Voyager 2 launched 16 days before its twin, Voyager 1.
Voyager 1 reached Jupiter and Saturn sooner than Voyager 2 because it was on a shorter and faster trajectory.
The mission relied on a rare planetary alignment that occurs approximately every 175 to 176 years.
Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to have visited the ice giant planets, Uranus and Neptune.
The probe utilized gravity assists from the giant planets to increase its velocity and reach its targets.
Voyager 2 entered interstellar space in November 2018.
The spacecraft is powered by three radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs) containing plutonium.
Voyager 2 carries a Golden Record with sounds and images of Earth intended for potential extraterrestrial discovery.
The probe has millions of times less memory than a modern smartphone.
Voyager 2 discovered active volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io.
The mission discovered that Jupiter has a ring system.
Images from the probe revealed that Jupiter's moon Europa has a cracked icy surface.
Voyager 2 discovered at least 10 previously unknown moons during its flyby of Uranus.
The mission discovered new rings around both Uranus and Neptune.
NASA can only send commands to Voyager 2 via the Deep Space Station 43 (DSS 43) antenna in Australia.
Northern hemisphere antennas cannot reach the probe because its path past Neptune steered it significantly southward.
The mission was originally part of a 'Grand Tour' concept that was scaled back by Congress due to costs.
The probe discovered Neptune's largest moon, Triton, has a surface temperature of -391 degrees Fahrenheit.

disputed: The number of moons discovered at Uranus: one source claims 11 (S1) while another says 10 (S4). Script should say 'at least 10'.
Launch interval: one source says 16 days (S1) while another says 'within 15 days' (S4). Script should say 'roughly two weeks'.
Alignment frequency: sources vary between 175 years (S2) and 176 years (S4). Script should say 'once every 176 years' or 'nearly 180 years'.
